key_insight: EmbodiedRSI improves robot adaptation by actively choosing informative physical experiments to co-evolve code, skills, and memory through a fast-slow hypothesis-driven loop.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to reduce costly teleoperation by making post-training more sample-efficient and transferable to real-world robot deployment.
method: Maintains competing code and skill hypotheses in a Hypothesis Graph
Uses Value-of-Information experiment selection to pick robot trials that best distinguish hypotheses
Updates policies through Code-Skill Co-Evolution plus Hierarchical Memory and Reward-Grounded Memory Learning
evidence_signal: On RoboCasa365, it achieved 77.0% overall success and 71.3% on Composite-Unseen versus 40.1% for the best baseline, and it also reached 86.8% on LIBERO-Pro with zero-shot real-world transfer at 71.3% overall success.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurately estimating which experiments have high value of information, which may be challenging when robot interactions are noisy, expensive, or safety-constrained.
paper_title: EmbodiedRSI: Active Continual Robot Learning Through Hypothesis-Guided Co-Evolution
